papers.title: Interpretable morphology-based marked statistics
papers.micro: Neural marked statistics thus offer a route to extracting non-Gaussian information from cosmological surveys, combining interpretable, physically motivated transformations with the practical advantages of two-point estimators.
papers.abstract: The shapes and environments of cosmic structures carry cosmological information beyond the matter power spectrum. Recovering this information while retaining a physical understanding is a central challenge for cosmological inference. We construct an interpretable, rotation-equivariant neural marking scheme that reweights the matter field, combining learned density responses with explicit measures of local morphology. This approach enables direct inspection of the learned transformations, while retaining the advantages of a two-point function analysis. We employ a contrastive learning framework to align the marked summaries with the respective cosmological parameters. In real-space matter simulations, the learned marked spectra recover information beyond the ordinary power spectrum, tightening marginalized Fisher constraints on σ₈ and Ωm by factors of 1.7× and 1.5× relative to the power spectrum plus bispectrum at kmax=0.3 h Mpc⁻¹. Without retraining, our mark also improves a neutrino-mass forecast by a factor of 1.5× relative to the power spectrum at the same scale cut. Across the cosmological prior, our marking scheme also improve the prediction errors in both parameters by 1.3× over the best tested classical mark at kmax=0.2 h Mpc⁻¹. A qualitative comparison with neural forecasts motivates the possibility that these different compressions approach a common information level. Neural marked statistics thus offer a route to extracting non-Gaussian information from cosmological surveys, combining interpretable, physically motivated transformations with the practical advantages of two-point estimators.

papers.title: The Gamma-ray Luminosity Function of Fermi BL Lacertae Objects
papers.micro: Gamma-ray selected BL Lacs and FSRQs evolve similarly depending on their luminosities.
papers.abstract: We have used the largest sample of gamma-ray-selected Fermi BL Lacertae objects (1035 BL Lacs) ever used to determine the luminosity function and its evolution through cosmic time. This sample has its survey biases and selection effects well studied and a robust calculation of its detection efficiency. It spans a large range in luminosity (L_γ,min = 5.71×10⁴⁰ erg s⁻¹ and L_γ,max = 1.76×10⁴⁸ erg s⁻¹) and redshift ( 0 < z ≲ 4). We find that the local luminosity function follows a double power law. The density evolution of BL Lacs depends on the luminosity of the objects, with low-luminosity objects showing negative evolution (i.e., they are less common in the past) and high-luminosity objects showing positive evolution (i.e., they are more common in the past). We confirm that gamma-ray selected BL Lacs and FSRQs evolve similarly depending on their luminosities.

papers.title: Probabilistic, facility-specific prioritisation of temperate exoplanets for atmospheric characterisation with JWST and the ELT
papers.micro: We present an open Monte Carlo framework (UHI v6.1) that builds probabilistic priority lists separately for each facility and composition class, never as a single ranking.
papers.abstract: Deciding which temperate exoplanets to observe first matters for JWST transit spectroscopy and for planned ELT reflected-light instruments, yet signal-to-noise metrics ignore habitability and similarity indices ignore observability. We present an open Monte Carlo framework (UHI v6.1) that builds probabilistic priority lists separately for each facility and composition class, never as a single ranking. For each of 6,112 planets in the NASA Exoplanet Archive, 10,000 draws carry catalogue uncertainties through climate, cumulative stellar-XUV atmospheric retention, per-draw rocky, Hycean or gas-rich classes, and a JWST (transiting) or ELT/PCS (non-transiting) detection model, giving each planet a survival probability, a conditional score and a top-N probability. At 5σ, 255 rocky and 71 Hycean candidates remain viable. A Saltelli–Sobol analysis of 32 assumptions (N = 512) shows that the location and width of the XUV shoreline dominate the rocky lists, with total-order indices of 0.22 and 0.12 at 5σ (0.25 and 0.14 at 3σ), and all ten leading indices have 95% bootstrap half-widths below 0.05. For Hycean planets most outputs are degenerate and the analysis does not converge, so that branch is reported as indicative. Membership of these lists is limited mainly by whether a planet survives the habitability vetoes: at 5σ, 3 of the nominal JWST and 4 of the nominal ELT rocky top-10 targets enter the top 10 in at least half of all draws, yet every one of them stays in the top 10 in more than half of the draws in which it survives. Code, per-planet posterior summaries, sensitivity tables and maps are public, so observers can rerun the lists under their own instrument assumptions and see which inputs would most change a target's priority.

papers.title: Four consistent estimates of H₀ from a ΛCDM inference network given CMB data
papers.micro: The redundancy in H₀ determinations illuminates a hurdle to resolving the H₀ tension with alternative cosmological models.
papers.abstract: We organize inferences from cosmic microwave background (CMB) data, of the current rate of expansion, H₀, into a network whose structure is informed by a scaling symmetry of the Einstein-Boltzmann evolution equations. There are four distinct routes through this network from a calibrating anchor to H₀. Given key assumptions of the ΛCDM model, they are mutually consistent. This consistency is a significant feature of the ΛCDM model's compatibility with CMB data. The redundancy in H₀ determinations illuminates a hurdle to resolving the H₀ tension with alternative cosmological models.

papers.title: JAISP: A Joint Rubin-Euclid Foundation Model for Cross-Instrument Source Detection and Astrometry
papers.micro: We introduce JAISP (Joint AI Survey Processing), a foundation model that learns a single representation of ten-band imaging…
papers.abstract: Joint pixel-level processing of Rubin and Euclid imaging promises deeper source detection and the cross-survey consistency that precision cosmology requires. We introduce JAISP (Joint AI Survey Processing), a foundation model that learns a single representation of ten-band imaging: Rubin ugrizy and Euclid VIS, Y, J, and H, from the first public releases over ≈ 0.2 deg² of the ECDFS deep field. Trained without labels by predicting each band from the other nine, its frozen encoder drives small task-specific networks for source detection and astrometry. The detection network recovers nearly all VIS-selected Euclid Q1 catalog sources on held-out sky, and source injection shows that combining all ten bands extends the point-source detection limit by ≈ 0.3 mag beyond VIS alone. The astrometry network transfers the sharp VIS localization to the other nine bands, reducing median cross-band positional offsets from ≈ 50 to 6–10 mas while retaining the full precision of its VIS centroid anchor even for faint sources. Separating this per-source scatter exposes the cross-survey concordance field: a coherent 9–10 mas offset between the two independently Gaia-registered astrometric solutions, dominated by a component common to all bands. Applied without retraining to a second Euclid Deep Field, both networks perform without measurable loss. These gains serve the joint-survey science case: a deeper census recovers faint neighbors whose blending biases weak-lensing shapes and photometric redshifts, and VIS-grade positions in every band supply the common astrometric reference that joint photometry and faint-source proper motions require. A single representation learned once from survey pixels thus serves several measurements across the sky.

papers.title: VLT, Keck, and Gemini characterization of the temporarily captured flyby 2026 QQ₈
papers.micro: The paired survival difference (radiation pressure plus gravity minus gravity only) is  2 percentage points.
papers.abstract: Very Large Telescope, Keck I, and Gemini North photometry of 2026 QQ₈ on November 7-21 gives Sloan Digital Sky Survey-equivalent colors g−r=0.594^+0.056_−0.053, g−i=0.840^+0.066_−0.065, and i−z=−0.104^+0.067_−0.057 mag. Apollo 17 basalt slabs 75075,197 and 71055,239 fit the colors (reduced χ² of 0.57 and 0.89). The Bus-DeMeo Sq- and K-type templates give reduced χ²=0.87 and 0.90, respectively. The colors permit both an Sq-like asteroid and exposed lunar basalt. With revised Keck timing uncertainties, 71 positions (August 19-November 21) give an outward acceleration of (1.363±0.090)×10⁻¹⁰ au day⁻² at 1 au, implying an area-to-mass ratio of (6.02±0.40)×10⁻⁴ m² kg⁻¹ for a unit radiation-pressure coefficient. For pre-encounter analogues, NEOMOD3 assigns source probabilities of 78.8% to the ν₆ resonance and 20.6% to Jupiter's 3:1 resonance. For a sphere with H=31.37±0.34, the diameter, density, and mass are (1.44^+0.28_−0.23 m, 1.73^+0.36_−0.30 g cm⁻³, 2.73^+1.19_−0.82×10³ kg) for the Sq albedo (pV=0.243±0.039), (1.62^+0.28_−0.24 m, 1.54^+0.29_−0.24 g cm⁻³, 3.43^+1.30_−0.94×10³ kg) for NEOMOD3 (pV=0.191), and (2.49^+0.42_−0.36 m, 1.00^+0.19_−0.16 g cm⁻³, 8.09^+3.06_−2.22×10³ kg) for lunar slabs (pV=0.081). With radiation pressure, nominal capture lasts 224.96 days (April 26-December 7). Sun-Earth corotating geocentric longitude advances 0.76 turns, classifying 2026 QQ₈ as a temporarily captured flyby. Its three-dimensional corotating path tangent turns 1.33 revolutions. After 10,000 yr, about 800 of 1,000 clones survive in each model, with about 200 colliding with Earth. The paired survival difference (radiation pressure plus gravity minus gravity only) is  2 percentage points.

papers.title: Euclid Data Release 1 (DR1). Learning machine learning: Investigating the complementarity and biases of strong gravitational lens finding networks on Euclid data
papers.micro: On the full DR1 sample, we show that individual networks have distinct biases: some networks favour systems with a larger Einstein radius while others are more sensitive to compact configurations.
papers.abstract: The Euclid Data Release 1 (DR1) strong lens search presents ECLIPSE, the largest catalogue of strong gravitational lens candidates to date, with >15 000 systems identified across 1900 deg2 of sky. It was constructed using five neural networks applied to approximately 68 million galaxies, followed by citizen science and expert visual inspection. In this work, we compare how the independently developed networks use image information to identify their selection of strong lens candidates. The search combines convolutional neural networks and a vision transformer, using the same pool of data but with different image processing and training choices. We investigate why these networks find different systems and what that means for the completeness of our catalogue. We evaluate all networks on a 50 deg2 calibration set and their application to the full DR1 sample. We find that the networks score candidates very differently, and that combining them recovers over 500 lens candidates within our calibration set at an inspection budget of 2000 objects. On the full DR1 sample, we show that individual networks have distinct biases: some networks favour systems with a larger Einstein radius while others are more sensitive to compact configurations. We also investigate network preferences in terms of lens light profile, mass distribution geometry, photometric redshift, and magnitudes. These findings provide a detailed analysis of how neural network selection biases have shaped the Euclid DR1 ECLIPSE catalogue. The results inform how networks should be combined in future Euclid data releases and upcoming wide-field surveys such as LSST or Roman to maximise both completeness and diversity of the recovered lens population.

papers.title: The Simons Observatory: Analysis of methods for polarization calibration of multiple instruments
papers.micro: For β=0.3°, we show how the LAT's ℓ-range distinguishes scale-independent dark-energy rotation from scale-dependent axion dark-matter models via Cℓ^EB.
papers.abstract: Cosmic birefringence, the rotation of the CMB linear polarization plane across the Universe, is a powerful test of parity-violating physics beyond the Standard Model. Static isotropic rotation, however, is limited by an instrument's absolute polarization-angle calibration. We present a method for transferring absolute calibration between Simons Observatory (SO) instruments, validated on map-level simulations of the Large Aperture Telescope (LAT) and Small Aperture Telescopes (SATs) with lensed CMB polarization, polarized Galactic foregrounds, correlated instrumental noise, and polarization-angle miscalibration. We develop two pipelines: a joint LAT+SAT likelihood transferring calibration through their overlap, and the Minami-Komatsu foreground-based method, which separates cosmic birefringence from instrumental miscalibration using Galactic dust polarization without an external angle prior. We derive a general variance budget showing that calibration transfer improves sensitivity only when the combined reference and overlap transfer uncertainties remain below the receiving instrument's calibration uncertainty. While transfer does not lower the absolute-angle floor for isotropic β, it anchors the receiving instrument's multipole range. The relative-angle uncertainty is ∼ 0.1° for ℓmax^SAT=300, improving to ∼ 0.04° at ℓmax^SAT=600, subject to SAT beam and transfer-function control. Finally, for β=0.3°, we show how the LAT's ℓ-range distinguishes scale-independent dark-energy rotation from scale-dependent axion dark-matter models via Cℓ^EB.

papers.title: Magnetic Reconnection and High-Speed Jets Downstream of a Parallel Shock: Full Particle-in-cell Simulations
papers.micro: For the first time, we report a systematic mass-ratio dependence of HSJ morphology in full PIC simulations…
papers.abstract: Collisionless shocks are of fundamental interest in astrophysics and space physics as important sources of energetic particles. Downstream of quasi-parallel shocks, high-speed jets (HSJs) and magnetic reconnection have been frequently observed, while it remains unclear how their coupling shapes structured regions for particle energization. We use two-dimensional full particle-in-cell simulations to investigate HSJ generation, thin current sheet formation, and associated electron energization downstream of a parallel shock. We find that portions of foreshock ULF waves with enhanced dynamic pressure interact with a self-reforming shock front and are transmitted downstream, forming HSJs, while neighboring low pressure portions evolve into cavities. At the leading edge of the HSJs, the unique bent magnetic topology carried by the compressed ULF waves produces bow waves and locally squeezes out thin current sheets. These current sheets show reconnection signatures, including X-point topology, magnetic islands, enhanced J· E', and Alfvenic outflows along the local reconnecting direction. In the reconnection region associated with HSJs, the parallel electric field, betatron, and Fermi terms all contribute to adiabatic electron energization. The betatron term appears a visible signature near the X line, where the local magnetic structure is compressed by the HSJ. For the first time, we report a systematic mass-ratio dependence of HSJ morphology in full PIC simulations: lower mass ratios produce fragmented HSJs with shorter lifetimes, whereas larger mass ratios yield longer and wider HSJs with clearer bow waves as ion inertia increases.
papers.caption: Overview of HSJs at a parallel shock.

papers.title: Primordial black holes production in Einstein-Gauss-Bonnet gravity
papers.micro: Due to estimation of possiable PBHs masses, we demonstrate that they can be considered as a possible source for all or part of dark matter.
papers.abstract: We consider models with the Gauss-Bonnet term multiplied to a function of the scalar field and propose a new inflationary model which provides a mechanism for the formation of primordial black holes (PBHs). For certain values of the model parameters, the predictions of this model agree with observational data from the Atacama Cosmology Telescope (ACT). Due to estimation of possiable PBHs masses, we demonstrate that they can be considered as a possible source for all or part of dark matter.

papers.title: Revealing Dark Matter in the Dark-Electron Rate of Xenon Detectors
papers.micro: Dramatic gains in sensitivity are possible, motivating new analyses of present and future xenon data.
papers.abstract: There is high interest in improving experimental sensitivity to sub-GeV dark matter (DM) that scatters with electrons, as compelling theoretical models seem within reach. At the lowest DM masses, most of the expected signal lies in the single-electron regime, but so do large backgrounds. Xenon experiments therefore either do not yet search there at all or, as in XENONnT, apply cuts so severe that only ∼10^-4 of the exposure is retained, with sensitivity set by the criterion S ≲ B, where those are the signal and background counts. We advocate that xenon detectors instead utilize most of their dark−electron rate (i.e., the total raw electron hit rate) and perform an annual−modulation search, for which the sensitivity scales as S ≲ √B. Modern DAQs already record this rate, continuously in triggerless systems such as the XENONnT and PandaX−4T DAQs, and within trigger windows in LZ, so no new hardware is required. Using measured dark−electron rates, we estimate the sensitivity of XENONnT, LZ, PandaX−4T, PandaX−xT, and XLZD. We find that dramatic gains in sensitivity are possible, motivating new analyses of present and future xenon data.

papers.title: Higgs-portal dark matter beyond kinetic equilibrium
papers.micro: We find the full momentum-dependent results systematically strengthen the direct detection constraints.
papers.abstract: We revisit the scalar, vector, and fermion Higgs-portal dark matter models in the resonant regime without assuming kinetic equilibrium during the freeze-out. We compute the relic abundance by solving the full momentum-dependent Boltzmann equation and compare the results with the standard momentum-averaged treatment. We find that the standard treatment significantly underestimates the relic abundance below the resonance, apart from the fermionic case with a purely scalar portal coupling where the difference is negligible. The deviation from the standard treatment is largest for fermionic models with pseudoscalar interactions, corresponding to factor of 10 in terms of the coupling that reproduces the correct relic abundance. For the scalar and vector cases the corresponding difference is up to a factor of 2. We confront the resulting parameter space with the latest constraints from direct and indirect detection, as well as collider experiments. We find the full momentum-dependent results systematically strengthen the direct detection constraints.

papers.title: Kinetic moment estimates and a one-sided Lyapunov barrier for the relativistic fermionic Michie-King equation
papers.micro: We also identify and correct a logarithmic coefficient in the previously used explicit linear-comparator formula.
papers.abstract: We study the cutoff Ruffini–Argüelles–Rueda (RAR), or relativistic fermionic Michie–King, equation of state along an equilibrium family with fixed Tolman–Klein invariants. Three kinetic moments give exact formulas for both the pressure-to-density ratio and the derivative of pressure. Cauchy–Schwarz yields a global relation between these two quantities. It implies vertical vector-field domination of the associated Tolman–Oppenheimer–Volkoff system by the linear equation of state P=ρc²/√3 in the physical wedge 0<y≤3x. We construct a filled, one-sided version of the Bors–Stańczy Lyapunov barrier and check every boundary. This controls all outward excursions, including those after a lower exit from a Lyapunov sublevel. For regular configurations the resulting explicit Lambert bound is 2Gm(r)/(rc²)<0.6879212521. Using the diagonal where this ratio has a stationary value sharpens the bound to 0.6734385929. The argument is conditional on a regular TOV configuration and does not require a separate finite-radius existence theorem. We also identify and correct a logarithmic coefficient in the previously used explicit linear-comparator formula.

papers.title: Finite-Temperature Stabilization of a KKLT Modulus in Three-Dimensional Lattice Simulations
papers.micro: These results demonstrate that capture of the spatially averaged modulus does not guarantee that every spatial region remains within the stabilizing barrier.
papers.abstract: We investigate the cosmological stabilization of a KKLT modulus through three-dimensional Langevin lattice simulations incorporating an evolving thermal bath, dissipation, spatial gradients, and stochastic fluctuations. While the spatially averaged modulus closely follows homogeneous evolution away from the capture threshold, near-critical trajectories linger near the unstable potential barrier for approximately one e-fold, allowing long-wavelength fluctuations to undergo tachyonic amplification and drive localized regions across the barrier even as the mean field turns back toward the stabilized vacuum. Linear Langevin theory reproduces the fluctuation growth, while convergence tests identify a narrow stochastic layer in which the barrier-crossing fraction shows no systematic dependence on the discretization at a fixed effective distance from the threshold. These results demonstrate that capture of the spatially averaged modulus does not guarantee that every spatial region remains within the stabilizing barrier.

papers.title: Quantifying the Impact of Galactic Dark Matter Halo Models on LZ Results
papers.micro: These results show that halo-model dependence is modest at high WIMP masses but becomes essential near kinematic thresholds.
papers.abstract: Most dark matter direct-detection limits are reported under the assumption of an isotropic, Maxwellian Standard Halo Model. However, the Milky Way's stellar halo exhibits substantial radial anisotropy, while cosmological simulations predict scale-dependent anisotropy in the dark matter velocity distribution. We investigate how departures from isotropy affect the interpretation of LZ results in two complementary regimes: background-dominated elastic-scattering searches and the recently reported 248 keV nuclear-recoil candidate, which we study using a background-free single-event approximation. For elastic scattering, we use the self-consistent isotropic, Osipkov-Merritt, axisymmetric, and triaxial halo models of Belli et al. and translate the published limits through the ratio of predicted event counts, applying a common escape-speed truncation in the Galactic frame. At WIMP masses above approximately 40 GeV, the resulting limits lie within about ± 30% of the isotropic reference. Below approximately 15 GeV, the model envelope broadens to as much as an order of magnitude, reflecting sensitivity to the high-velocity tail. For the 248 keV event, the accessible inelastic mass splitting is likewise controlled by this tail. Some anisotropic models extend the allowed kinematic region towards splittings at which solar-neutrino constraints on a Higgsino interpretation become ineffective, although kinematic accessibility alone does not establish viability at the fixed Higgsino cross section. These results show that halo-model dependence is modest at high WIMP masses but becomes essential near kinematic thresholds.

papers.title: A novel mechanism for coherent radio emission: particle-in-cell simulations
papers.micro: This study provides new insights into the wave excitation, the nonlinear wave-particle interactions…
papers.abstract: It has been established that electron (phase-space) holes, i.e., EHs, can arise from the nonlinear relaxation of the electron beam instability. Excitation of electromagnetic waves related to the EHs is, however, still not fully understood. Using 2.5-dimensional particle-in-cell simulations, we systematically investigate the nonlinear evolution of the (moderately relativistic) electron bi-stream instability (a special case of the electron beam instability where the densities of the two counter-propagating energetic electron beams are equivalent) in charge- and current-neutralized plasmas under weak and strong magnetizations. This study provides new insights into the wave excitation, the nonlinear wave-particle interactions, the formation of non-Maxwellian features, and the anisotropic electron heating in magnetized plasmas, with potential implications for coherent radio emission in astrophysical plasmas (e.g., solar zebra-pattern bursts).
papers.caption: Panel [ a ] presents the temporal evolution of the drift velocity of the electron bi-streams.

papers.title: Radial Evolution of Correlation Anisotropy in PUNCH Observations of the Young Solar Wind
papers.micro: In this way, the very large field of view of PUNCH images reveal a fundamental transition of solar wind turbulence toward isotropy.
papers.abstract: Solar wind turbulence, evolving in the presence of a mean magnetic field, large-scale shear, and expansion, exhibits several types of anisotropy, including wavevector anisotropy and variance anisotropy. As the solar wind expands from the corona into the interplanetary space, the magnetically controlled outer corona transitions into the dynamic and less constrained solar wind, and fluctuations may evolve toward isotropy. This is suggestive of an evolution of anisotropy with distance from the Sun, a feature observed in earlier results using surveys of in-situ data, as well as more limited images of solar wind density from STEREO. Here we confirm and expand on those results employing data from the PUNCH mission, whose wide-field, high-cadence imaging enables anisotropy tracking at different heliospheric positions. We evaluate a two-dimensional (2D) correlation function C(ℓ⊥, ℓ∥) of polarized white-light brightness as a function of radial ℓ∥ and transverse ℓ⊥ scales to infer the nature of density anisotropy and its development in space. At larger heliocentric distances (∼ 100 R☉), circular contours of the correlation function indicate a transition toward approximate isotropy. The correlation structure at heliocentric distances from 30R☉ to 60R☉ preferentially extends along the radial direction, which might imply the possible dominance of the two-dimensional variation in the transverse plane. In this way, the very large field of view of PUNCH images reveal a fundamental transition of solar wind turbulence toward isotropy.

papers.title: Gravitational waves in hierarchical triples with lensing and relativistic orbits
papers.micro: This method improves the accuracy of such a triple waveform significantly compared to previous post-Newtonian approximations, and allows numerically efficient computation of the modulations.
papers.abstract: Binary black holes (BBH) may be formed near galactic nuclei. If such BBH systems exist, modulations to the gravitational waveform through time delays, lensing, and angular momentum precession could allow the presence of the third body to be measured in this system. In this letter, we advance the modeling for hierarchical triples by carefully including new relativistic lensing, aberration, and polarization terms. We show that the gravitational waves from this system can be computed exactly in the geometric optics limit by ray tracing the null geodesics and parallel transporting their polarization without a weak-field expansion. Our construction evolves the inner binary as if it were a post-Newtonian signal, and computes the environmental modulations efficiently with elliptic integrals. We find that this method improves the accuracy of such a triple waveform significantly compared to previous post-Newtonian approximations, and allows numerically efficient computation of the modulations. This lays the groundwork for future hierarchical triple waveform codebases, which can be used in LISA parameter estimation and detectability.

papers.title: Pseudoscalar Yukawa Preheating via Effective Action Approach
papers.micro: By integrating out the fermionic fields and employing the Schwinger proper time representation…
papers.abstract: In this work, we investigate helicity-dependent fermion production driven by a pseudoscalar Yukawa interaction within the one-loop effective action framework. By integrating out the fermionic fields and employing the Schwinger proper time representation, we derive an analytical expression for the fermion pair production probability near each zero crossing of the oscillating inflaton field. We further introduce a helicity transfer matrix to describe the evolution of fermionic modes through successive non-adiabatic production events. For an undamped inflaton background, the temporal symmetry around successive zero crossings leads to the cancellation of helicity-mixing contributions after an even number of events, preventing the accumulation of helicity asymmetry. We then extend the analysis to a damped oscillatory background, in which the decreasing inflaton amplitude breaks this temporal symmetry and modifies the transfer matrix at each crossing. The resulting non-commuting transfer matrices produce a persistent helical spectrum, as demonstrated by the probabilities as a function of momentum obtained after successive scattering events. A comparison with scalar Yukawa preheating further confirms the role of helicity mixing in generating the helical asymmetry induced by pseudoscalar mechanism. These results establish an effective action framework for studying helicity asymmetry during fermionic preheating and provide insight into the influence of the inflaton's dynamical evolution on particle production.

papers.title: Revisiting RadioGalaxyNET: modern detectors for radio galaxy detection and host identification
papers.micro: Future work report host identification F1, as a measure closer to catalog use: D-FINE-seg M 71.8, YOLO26-pose M 70.5, RF-DETR 63.8, Gal-DINO 59.2.
papers.abstract: RadioGalaxyNET is the public benchmark for finding extended radio galaxies in EMU pilot-survey images, classifying them and locating their infrared hosts. Its best published results date from 2023: 54.5 box AP (Gal-YOLOv8) and 48.1 host keypoint AP (Gal-DINO). We train three current detectors, D-FINE-seg, YOLO26-pose and RF-DETR, on the same data and score them with the benchmark's own evaluation code, which reproduces the published Gal-DINO numbers exactly. All exceed the published results. D-FINE-seg M reaches 67.1 box AP and 72.4 host AP, 12.6 and 24.3 points above the best published results, and the highest host AP of the detectors we tested; on boxes it is level with YOLO26. Its host lead over YOLO26 comes from host-centered images, which make up most of the benchmark. End to end, D-FINE-seg S is the fastest model at 1.9 ms per image; engine against engine, YOLO26 is faster at the same size. We also report what matters for anyone using the benchmark: its scoring protocol adds 5 to 10 AP, its host labels sit at the image center, its box labels are offset from the image by 1.5 pixels, and its images can be rebuilt from the public survey data, which recovers sky positions and doubles as extra training data. We suggest that future work report host identification F1, as a measure closer to catalog use: D-FINE-seg M 71.8, YOLO26-pose M 70.5, RF-DETR 63.8, Gal-DINO 59.2.

papers.title: World Models Are the Right Foundation for Simulating Mars Terraforming
papers.micro: We also introduce MarsWorld, an open benchmark proposal for intervention-conditioned planetary world models, and discuss broader implications and objections.
papers.abstract: Terraforming Mars is a long-horizon, action-conditioned control problem that requires predicting atmospheric responses to interventions over centuries to identify effective policies. This position paper argues that physics-regularized recurrent state-space world models are the most promising foundation for this setting. Data-driven climate emulators lack action-conditioning, and physics-based general circulation models (GCMs) are too expensive for policy search. Among learned world models, recurrent state-space architectures with physics constraints are better suited than transformer-based alternatives: they provide native uncertainty quantification through their stochastic-deterministic decomposition, remain stable under sparse non-terrestrial training data, and enforce physical consistency at each rollout step. To make this position concrete, we describe a potential architecture combining JEPA-inspired latent encoding, universal differential equation constraints, and a Dreamer-lineage planning head. We also introduce MarsWorld, an open benchmark proposal for intervention-conditioned planetary world models, and discuss broader implications and objections.

papers.title: Superheavy gravitational dark matter from runaway bubble collisions
papers.micro: Gravity alone then gives dark matter up to about 10¹⁷ GeV at reheating temperatures far below its mass, where freeze-in fails.
papers.abstract: A stable particle that couples only through gravity is pair-produced in collisions of runaway bubble walls by graviton exchange. For a transition of duration 1/β, a Dirac fermion reaches the yield YX≃6.8×10⁻³(H/β)(Treh/MP)³, where H is the Hubble rate of the vacuum energy, Treh the reheating temperature and MP the reduced Planck mass. The yield is flat up to masses near (H/β)MP/ν², where ν of order one sets the wall-field excursion. Gravity alone then gives dark matter up to about 10¹⁷ GeV at reheating temperatures far below its mass, where freeze-in fails.

papers.title: Post-Newtonian expansion of the energy and angular momentum flux radiated to infinity: Eccentric-equatorial orbits about a Kerr black hole
papers.micro: We obtain the expressions using the method of Mano, Suzuki, and Takasugi, which provides infinite-series analytical solutions to the Teukolsky equation that we generate using Mathematica.
papers.abstract: We present analytical expressions for the energy and angular momentum fluxes radiated to infinity by a (nonspinning) point mass in an eccentric-equatorial orbit about a Kerr black hole. These results build upon our previous work involving point masses on eccentric orbits about a Schwarzschild black hole. We now adopt the Teukolsky formalism in first-order black hole perturbation theory to extend our methods to Kerr. We obtain the expressions using the method of Mano, Suzuki, and Takasugi, which provides infinite-series analytical solutions to the Teukolsky equation that we generate using Mathematica. The expressions presented are obtained as a double expansion in the post-Newtonian (PN) compactness parameter 1/p, where p is the dimensionless semi-latus rectum, and in the eccentricity e, up to 10PN and e²⁰, extending beyond prior 6PN and e¹⁶ results available for generic orbits. We characterize how the PN flux coefficients depend on the black hole spin a and e, and find a set of spin-dependent components that can be resummed as closed-form expressions in e. The analytical expressions are then validated with numerical comparisons against high-precision sample results from an independent Teukolsky code and with a broader set of numerically interpolated values derived from a flux data set produced with the same code. For a=0.9M, the numerically evaluated 10PN fluxes match current interpolated flux grids (∼10⁻⁷) for p≳20 to 75 as e ranges from 0.1 to 0.7, where they could replace Teukolsky-code results.

papers.title: Dissipative Tidal Love Numbers of Neutron Stars from Viscous Heating
papers.micro: The first method reduces the calculation to an integral over the static equilibrium tide; the second provides an independent check.
papers.abstract: We compute the leading low-frequency dissipative tidal response of nonrotating relativistic neutron stars. We formulate the response in a worldline effective field theory. We determine the linear dissipative Love number in two complementary ways: from the redshifted viscous entropy production inside the star and from the imaginary, frequency-odd part of the exterior metric. The first method reduces the calculation to an integral over the static equilibrium tide; the second provides an independent check. We apply our approach to publicly available equations of state and assess the corresponding correction to the gravitational-wave phase of neutron-star binaries. For an equal-mass 1.4+1.4M☉ binary with both stars at a redshifted temperature T∞=10⁵ K and a standard electron shear viscosity, tidal dissipation shifts the gravitational-wave phase by less than 10⁻³ cycles between 20  Hz and 1  kHz for the four equations of state considered. Including the resulting rise in the stars' temperature in a simple thermal model reduces the shift below 10⁻⁶ cycles. For the viscosity model considered here, shear-viscous tidal dissipation in cold neutron stars is negligible for gravitational-wave phasing. This suggests that a measurable dissipative tidal signature would have to come from a different mechanism.

papers.title: The Science Chapter of the Einstein Telescope Geometry Comparison Report
papers.micro: Differences between geometries shrink, but the ranking is largely unchanged.
papers.abstract: This is the Scientific Added Value Chapter of the Einstein Telescope (ET) Geometry Comparison Report, commissioned from the ET Organization by the ET Board of Governmental Representatives. We compare three configurations: a single-site 10-km triangle (Δ) and two 15-km L-shaped detectors (2L) at widely separated sites, either nearly aligned or misaligned. We use metrics representative of the ET science case: compact-binary populations, dense matter, cosmography, stochastic backgrounds, multimessenger astronomy, fundamental physics, and continuous and burst sources. All three configurations deliver the ET science case, but they excel in different areas. For most sensitivity-driven science, the 2L configurations outperform the Δ. The misaligned 2L is best for localizing and characterizing individual sources, multimessenger astronomy, and bright-siren cosmology. The nearly aligned 2L is best for stochastic backgrounds. The Δ localizes sources better than the aligned 2L and performs comparably to both 2L configurations for continuous and burst sources and at kilohertz frequencies. A 2L orientation of 30° is a good compromise between stochastic-background sensitivity and localization. We validate Fisher information matrix (FIM) forecasts against Bayesian inference for ∼550 binary black hole and neutron star-black hole signals. Despite substantial differences, the FIM shows no systematic preference for either configuration for intrinsic parameters. For distance and sky localization, the FIM cannot capture multimodality and long-range correlations, leading to larger discrepancies, which however do not affect the ranking. Adding Cosmic Explorer to the network improves the reach of all three ET configurations, especially in volume localization and characterization of high-redshift sources. Differences between geometries shrink, but the ranking is largely unchanged.

papers.title: Exact analytic solutions for the n=1 chameleon field in planar systems with an arbitrary number of uniform layers
papers.micro: We also use our solutions to forecast constraints from CANNEX, a recent experiment devised to measure Casimir forces and detect hypothetical fifth forces.
papers.abstract: Scalar fields have long been investigated as a potential dark energy candidate. Of these models, screened scalar fields like the chameleon have received interest due to their ability to avoid observational constraints. However, the non-linear nature of these models has led to there being only a small number of exact analytic solutions within the literature. In this work, we present exact analytic solutions for the n=1 chameleon model in a planar system consisting of N discrete regions of uniform density. We compare these to the relevant approximate solutions within the literature. We also use our solutions to forecast constraints from CANNEX, a recent experiment devised to measure Casimir forces and detect hypothetical fifth forces. Unlike in previous works, we consider the full fifteen-layered setup of CANNEX, as opposed to treating the plate and wall as single uniform objects. Doing so revealed an increase in the induced chameleon pressure of up to ∼ 7 %. However, the resulting gain is insufficient to probe new regions of parameter space at the projected sensitivities.

papers.title: Analytic k-essence Inflation
papers.micro: However, using qualitative and quantitative numerical arguments, we show that the pressure singularity is classically avoided when the matter fluids of radiation and cold dark matter are taken into account.
papers.abstract: In this work we develop a fully analytic k-essence inflation solution which is compatible with the observational constraints on inflation, without the need for the slow-roll assumption being imposed dynamically in the field equations. The analytic solution is obtained for a kinetic scalar sector of the form K(X)= Xⁿ/(Xsⁿ⁻¹) and for the scalar field satisfying a tracking condition φ²=γH⁻ᵐ. For this class of theories, the sound speed of the primordial curvature perturbations is constant, so no gradient instabilities occur in the theory. The Hubble rate, the scale factor and the scalar field can be analytically expressed as functions of the cosmic time, and the observational indices of inflation depend solely on the parameters n and m. The resulting evolution is inflationary and it develops a pressure singularity a few e-foldings after the end of inflation. However, using qualitative and quantitative numerical arguments, we show that the pressure singularity is classically avoided when the matter fluids of radiation and cold dark matter are taken into account.

papers.title: Relativistic dynamical friction and accretion for Kerr black holes
papers.micro: A similar reversal can be mimicked around a non-rotating BH if the initial halo carries large net angular momentum, although this requires anisotropies beyond those found in cosmological simulations.
papers.abstract: Extreme-mass-ratio inspirals (EMRIs) observed by LISA will probe the environments of massive black holes (BHs), including the dark matter (DM) overdensities expected to form around them. We compute the relativistic dynamical friction and accretion experienced by a non-spinning compact object on circular equatorial orbits around a Kerr BH embedded in a collisionless DM distribution, extending previous results in Schwarzschild. The DM is modeled as a spike grown adiabatically from an initial Hernquist profile, and the momentum transfer is obtained by integrating relativistic scattering and capture cross sections over the full, generically anisotropic phase space seen by the secondary. Far from the primary the friction tracks the local DM density, which increases with spin. Near the innermost stable circular orbit of rapidly spinning BHs (a≳ 0.37), however, frame dragging forces bound DM particles to co-rotate, so that the secondary is overtaken by the surrounding medium: the friction weakens and eventually reverses sign where the DM density peaks. We show that a similar reversal can be mimicked around a non-rotating BH if the initial halo carries large net angular momentum, although this requires anisotropies beyond those found in cosmological simulations. We also show that commonly used Chandrasekhar-like prescriptions, which depend only on the local density, can overestimate the friction force. Our results demonstrate that the full phase-space structure of the environment must be included when modeling DM effects on EMRIs.

papers.title: Enhancing eccentricity through tidal resonance in binary neutron star systems
papers.micro: These findings reveal an origin of eccentricity in binary neutron stars that is independent of their formation history and provide important information for modeling binary neutron star dynamics…
papers.abstract: Orbital eccentricity of binary neutron star systems is a key parameter to reveal their formation history. Since binaries formed in isolation are expected to circularize long before merger, measurable eccentricity suggests dynamical formation in dense stellar environments. However, using numerical-relativity simulations, we show that eccentricity can be introduced in the late inspiral of an initially quasicircular binary, due to the f-mode resonance of one of the stars. We simulate the merger of two highly spinning neutron stars, one star spinning prograde and the other retrograde. Persistent tidal resonance with the f mode of the retrograde-spinning star is observed, accompanied by a gradual change of its spin due to angular momentum transfer from the orbit. This spin change can be well explained by a simple resonance locking model that accounts for the spin-dependent shift of the f-mode frequency. These findings reveal an origin of eccentricity in binary neutron stars that is independent of their formation history and provide important information for modeling binary neutron star dynamics with rapidly spinning stars.

papers.title: Optimal Statistic for a Stochastic Gravitational Wave Background using Pulsar-Timing–Astrometry Cross Correlations
papers.micro: We estimate the signal-to-noise ratios from the correlation statistics and provide scaling laws in the weak- and intermediate-signal regimes.
papers.abstract: Astrometric measurements have emerged as a viable probe of gravitational waves (GWs), complementing pulsar timing searches by providing overlapping and higher GW frequency coverage. At its core, the search for GWs using astrometry is very similar to the search with pulsar timing data: GWs induce a change in pulse arrival times along the line of sight to a pulsar and a transverse angular deflection in the apparent position of a star. In analogy to pulsar timing, we develop a correlation statistic between pairs of stellar deflections for astrometry to search for a stochastic GW background. With a common formalism for both astrometry and pulsar timing, we also develop the cross-correlation statistic between stellar deflections and pulsar timing residuals. We estimate the signal-to-noise ratios from the correlation statistics and provide scaling laws in the weak- and intermediate-signal regimes.
